title: This book was printed in 868 AD and survived for over 1,100 years; how an ancient Chinese text became a landmark in printing history
description: The Diamond Sutra, a Buddhist text printed in 868 AD, is the oldest known printed book. This discovery emphasizes the significance of Chinese printing technology, which predates Johannes Gutenberg's methods. Printing techniques included woodblock printing, which was favored over movable type due to the complexity of Chinese characters. A hidden library in a desert cave preserved this scroll until it was found by a monk.

title: Why students in ancient China honoured teachers by gifting wild vegetables
description: While it is common for Chinese people to hold banquets for teachers upon graduation as a way of honouring them – a traditional value – in ancient China, students expressed their respect for teachers differently: by presenting them with vegetables. The tradition began in the Zhou dynasty (1046–256 BC). On the first day of school, students wore blue gowns and brought their teachers wild vegetables they had gathered themselves. title: Zurich Blue, a nano-pigment inspired by an ancient prototype
description: For medical imaging, innovative contrast agents are in high demand. Materials scientist Robert Nissler has therefore developed an ultra-bright near-infrared nano-pigment designed to provide high-resolution images of intricate brain structures. In ancient Egypt, the precursor to the copper-based Zurich Blue was already prized for its brilliant blue color.
